Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the seventy-fifth of the "Open Door" sessions (al-Bab al-Maftuh), which are held every Thursday of the week. This is the eighth Thursday of Jumada al-Ula in the year 1415 AH. We open this session with the tafsir of Surat al-Layl, where Allah, blessed and exalted is He, says:

﴿By the night when it covers (1), and by the day when it appears in brightness (2), and by Him who created the male and the female (3), indeed your efforts are diverse (4).﴾ [al-Layl 1-4]

So Allah, glorified and exalted, swears by the night "when it covers" (idha yaghsha); meaning: when it covers the earth and envelopes it with its darkness, because al-ghisha' (الغِشاء) means a covering.

ﷻ "By the day when it displays itself" — i.e., when it becomes manifest and clear, which occurs with the breaking of dawn (al-fajr), the light that precedes the rising of the sun. The sun is the sign of the day, just as the moon is the sign of the night.

ۚ﴿And by He who created the male and the female﴾ — that is: and by the creation of the male and the female, according to one of the two interpretations, which takes "mā" here as a verbal-noun particle (ma maṣdariyya). Or: and by He who created the male and the female, which is Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, according to the other interpretation. On the first meaning, Allah, glory be to Him, swears by the creation of the male and the female; and on the second, Allah, exalted is He, swears by Himself, because He is the one who created the male and the female.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 92, verse 4:

﴿Indeed, your efforts are diverse.﴾ Meaning: indeed, your deeds are diverse; that is, they are divided into great and varied categories.

So you see now that Allah swore by things that are opposites, concerning things that are opposites. Night is the opposite of day, the male is the opposite of the female, and striving is of two opposing kinds: good and evil. Thus what is sworn by and what is sworn about are in harmony, and this is one of the eloquent features of the Qur'an. It is as though Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is saying: the difference between night and day and between male and female is a clear matter that cannot be hidden; likewise, the deeds of people are varied and differ: some are righteous, some are corrupt, and some mix the righteous with the corrupt. All of this occurs by the decree of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah guides whomever He wills to the straight path.

Then he elaborated on this scattered effort, saying: ﴿As for him who gives and fears (Allah), (5) and affirms the best (reward), (6) We will indeed ease him toward ease.﴾ [al-Layl 5–7].

﴿As for him who gives﴾: that is, he gives what he has been commanded to give, whether of wealth, status, or knowledge.

﴿and fears (Allah)﴾: he guards against what he has been commanded to guard against of the forbidden things.

﴿and affirms the best (reward)﴾: that is, he affirms the best word, which is the word of Allah the Mighty and Majestic and the word of His Messenger; for the truest speech and the best speech is the speech of Allah the Mighty and Majestic.

﴿We will indeed ease him toward ease﴾: the sin (س) here is for emphasis (tahqiq); that is, whoever gives, fears (Allah), and affirms the best (reward), Allah the Mighty and Majestic will indeed ease him toward ease in all his affairs, in the affairs of his religion and his worldly life. For this reason you find that the easiest of people in action is the one who fears Allah the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿whoever gives and fears (Allah) (5) and affirms the best (reward)﴾, and whenever a person is more God-fearing, his affairs become easier for him. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him a way out of his affair, and ease﴾ [al-Talaq 4].

And whenever a person is further from Allah, his affairs become more difficult for him; for this reason He said:

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 92, verse 8–10:

﴿As for he who is stingy﴾ and does not give what he was commanded to give, ﴿and considers himself self-sufficient﴾ [al-Layl 8]: he considers himself independent of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and does not fear his Lord, but rather sees himself as free from the mercy of Allah, (we ask Allah for well-being and safety). ﴿And denies the best [reward]﴾ [al-Layl 9], i.e., the good word (al-qawlah al-husna), which is the word of Allah and His Messenger. ﴿We will ease him toward difficulty﴾ [al-Layl 10]: he will be eased toward hardship (al-'usra) in all his affairs.

However, Satan may come to a person and say: "We find that the disbelievers have their affairs made easy." It is said in reply: Yes, their affairs may be made easy, but their hearts are ablaze with fire, constriction and distress, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever Allah wills to mislead, He makes his breast tight and constricted, as if he were climbing into the sky﴾ [al-An'am 125]. Then, what they enjoy is only physical pleasure, not pleasure of the soul; and furthermore it is a burden upon them, because of the saying of Allah the Exalted about them: ﴿We will lead them step by step from where they do not know. And I will give them respite; indeed, My plan is firm﴾ [al-Qalam 44–45]. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Indeed Allah gives respite to the wrongdoer, until when He seizes him, He does not let him go," and then he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And thus is the seizure of your Lord when He seizes the cities while they are wrongdoing. Indeed, His seizure is painful and severe﴾ [Hud 102][[Agreed upon; al-Bukhari (4686), with his wording, and Muslim (2583 / 61), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. These people have had their good things hastened for them in their worldly life, yet this world is, in comparison to the Hereafter, a garden for them.

It is also related about Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani, the commentator of al-Bukhari in the commentary he named Fath al-Bari, and who was chief judge in Egypt, that one day he passed by while on his carriage pulled by mules, with people around him. He passed by a Jewish man who was a seller of ghee (samman), meaning one who sells butter and oil, and you know that the sellers of ghee and oil have dirty clothes and poor condition. So he stopped the carriage and said to Ibn Hajar: "Your Prophet says: 'The world is a prison for the believer and a paradise for the disbeliever'[[Related by Muslim (2956 / 1), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. So how can I be in this condition while you are in this condition?!" Ibn Hajar replied at once: "I am in a prison in comparison to what Allah the Exalted has prepared for the believers of reward and bliss, because the world in comparison to the Hereafter is nothing; as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The place of one of your whips in Paradise is better than the world and what is in it'[[Related by al-Bukhari (2892), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi (may Allah be pleased with him).]]. As for you," he said to the Jew, "you are in a paradise in comparison to what has been prepared for you of punishment if you die upon disbelief." The Jew was convinced by this, and it became the reason for his Islam, and he said: "I bear witness that there is no god but Allah, and I bear witness that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

Then He, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls into ruin﴾ [Al-Layl 11]. Meaning: what use will his wealth be to him when he withholds it and falls into ruin himself, that is, perishes? What good is wealth then? It avails him nothing.

Then He, Exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾ [Al-Layl 12]. This will come, God willing, in a future session.

Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad, and upon his family and companions, and upon those who follow them in goodness until the Day of Judgment.

To proceed: this is the seventy-sixth session of the meeting known as "The Open Door Meeting," which is held every Thursday of every week. Today is Thursday, the fifteenth of Jumada al-Ula in the year 1415 AH. We ask Allah, glorified and exalted, to make all of our meetings meetings of goodness and blessing. Indeed, He is capable of all things.

We begin this session with the explanation of the remainder of Surah "By the night when it covers" (al-Layl), where Allah, blessed and exalted, says: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance (12). And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾ [al-Layl 12-13].

As for His saying, the Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾, it contains a commitment from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, to make clear to creation what they may be guided by. The guidance intended here is the guidance of clarification and direction. Allah, exalted, committed Himself to clarifying this so that people would have no argument against Allah. This is like His saying, exalted: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you as We revealed to Noah and the prophets after him﴾ [an-Nisa 163], until He said: ﴿as messengers bearing good news and warning, so that mankind would have no argument against Allah after the messengers﴾ [an-Nisa 165]. Pay attention, brothers: the human intellect cannot independently attain knowledge of guidance. For this reason, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, committed Himself to clarifying guidance for the human being: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾.

It should be known that guidance is of two kinds. The first is the guidance of divine success (tawfiq), which no one can grant except Allah. The second is the guidance of direction and indication (irshad wa dalalah), which comes both from Allah and from creation: from the messengers and from the scholars. As Allah said to His Prophet, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family: ﴿And indeed, you guide to a straight path﴾ [ash-Shura 52]. As for the guidance of success, it belongs to Allah. No one can grant a person success in goodness, as Allah, exalted, said: ﴿Indeed, you do not guide whom you like, but Allah guides whom He wills﴾ [al-Qasas 56].

When we consider this noble verse, ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾, we find that Allah, exalted, has clarified everything. He has clarified what people must uphold in belief, what they must uphold in worship, what they must uphold in morals, what they must uphold in dealings, and what they must avoid in all of this. So much so that Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: "The Messenger of Allah, may Allah's blessings and peace be upon him and his family, passed away, and there was no bird flapping its wings in the sky except that he had mentioned to us knowledge of it."[[Recorded by Ahmad (21361) from Abu Dharr with the wording: Muhammad ﷺ left us, and no bird moves its wings in the sky except that he reminded us of knowledge concerning it.]] And a man from the polytheists said to Salman al-Farisi: "Your Prophet has taught you everything, even relieving yourselves." He said: "Yes, indeed. He taught us even relieving ourselves."[[Recorded by Muslim (262/57) from Salman, who said: It was said to him: "Your Prophet ﷺ has taught you everything, even relieving yourselves." He said: "Yes indeed. He forbade us to face the qiblah when relieving ourselves or urinating, or to clean ourselves with the right hand, or to clean ourselves with fewer than three stones, or to clean ourselves with dung or bone."]] That is: even the etiquette of relieving oneself, the Prophet ﷺ taught to his community. This is confirmed by the saying of Allah, exalted: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you, completed My favor upon you, and approved Islam as your religion﴾ [al-Ma'idah 3].

﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life].﴾ Meaning: to Us belong the Hereafter and the first [life]. The first [life] comes before the Hereafter in time, yet here He placed the Hereafter first. Why?

We say: for two benefits. The first benefit is semantic (ma'nawi), and the second is verbal (lafzi).

As for the semantic benefit, the Hereafter is more important than this world, and in the Hereafter the dominion of Allah, exalted is He, will appear in its entirety. In this world there are presidents, there are kings, and there are rulers who possess what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has given them of dominion. But in the Hereafter no one has dominion: ﴿Whose is the dominion this Day? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [Ghafir 16]. Therefore He mentioned the Hereafter first, for this semantic benefit.

As for the verbal benefit, it is observance of the fawasil (the rhyming verse-endings). That is, the endings of all these verses, as you see, end in alif: ﴿By the night when it covers (1), and the day when it appears in brightness﴾. So if He had said, "And indeed to Us belong the first and the Hereafter," the verse-endings would have differed. Therefore He said: ﴿And indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the first.﴾

Here it becomes clear that Allah, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿Upon Us is guidance (12), and indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the first.﴾ What is the difference?

The difference is that Allah, exalted is He, has bound Himself to clarify and make guidance manifest to creation. As for dominion, it belongs to Allah: the dominion of the Hereafter and of the first [life]. For this reason He said: ﴿And indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the first.﴾

Then the Mighty and Majestic said: ﴿So I have warned you of a Fire that blazes fiercely﴾ [al-Layl 14]. ﴿I have warned you﴾ means I have frightened you. "The Fire" here refers to the Fire of the Hereafter. ﴿Blazes fiercely﴾ means it flares up. It has many attributes mentioned in the Qur'an and the Sunnah. May Allah protect me and you from it.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 92, verse 15–16:

﴿None shall enter it except the most wretched﴾ [al-Layl: 15]. Meaning: none shall be burned in it except the most wretched; that is, the one for whom wretchedness (shaqawa) has been decreed—may Allah protect us—and wretchedness is the opposite of happiness (sa'ada), as in the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿As for those who were wretched, they will be in the Fire﴾ [Hud: 106], and His words: ﴿And as for those who were made happy, they will be in Paradise﴾ [Hud: 108]. So what is meant by ﴿the most wretched﴾ is the one for whom happiness was not written; this is the one who will enter the Fire that blazes.

Then He explained this by His words: ﴿who denied and turned away﴾ [al-Layl: 16]. Denial (al-takdhib) is in opposition to the report, and turning away (al-tawalli) is in opposition to the command and the prohibition. So this one denied the report and did not believe it. It was said to him: "Indeed you will be resurrected," and he said: "I will not be resurrected." It was said: "In it there is Paradise and Fire," and he said: "There is no Paradise or Fire in it." It was said: "Such and such will happen," and he said: "It will not happen." This is denial.

﴿Turned away﴾ means: he turned away from obedience to Allah and turned away from what His messengers brought. This is the most wretched. We ask Allah to protect us and you from wretchedness.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 92, verse 17:

﴿And the most righteous one will be kept away from it﴾: i.e., the one who is kept away from this Fire that blazes ﴿the most righteous﴾ [al-Layl 17]. ﴿Al-Atqa﴾ (the most righteous) is a superlative (ism tafdil) derived from taqwa (God-consciousness, piety); meaning: the one who fears Allah, the Exalted, with the fear that is due to Him.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 92, verse 18:

﴿The one who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾ [al-Layl: 18]. It means: he gives his wealth to one who deserves it, in a manner by which he purifies himself; i.e., he cleanses himself by it. Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Take from their wealth a charity by which you purify them and cause them to grow, and pray for them. Indeed, your prayer is a comfort for them﴾ [at-Tawbah: 103]. So His saying: ﴿The one who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾ indicates that he is neither a squanderer nor a miser, but gives wealth in a manner through which there is purification. The standard for this is what Allah mentioned in surah al-Furqan: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are ever, between that, justly moderate﴾ [al-Furqan: 67].

We find some people whom Allah has given wealth, yet they are stingy and niggardly, not even fulfilling what is obligatory upon them toward their wives, children and relatives. And we see some people whose provision Allah has restricted and whose means He has narrowed somewhat, yet despite that they go into debt from people in order to complete their house, so that it is like the house of so-and-so and so-and-so, or to buy a luxurious car like the car of so-and-so and so-and-so. Both of these approaches and paths are false: the first fell short, and the second went to excess. What is obligatory upon a person is that his spending be according to his condition: ﴿who gives his wealth to purify himself﴾.

If someone asks: Is it permissible for a person to go into debt in order to give charity?

The answer: No, because charity is voluntary, and taking on debt is a great danger, for debt is no light matter. When a person dies, his soul remains suspended by his debt until it is settled on his behalf.

Many heirs do not concern themselves with the debt of the deceased; you find them delaying, procrastinating, and perhaps never paying it—we ask Allah for safety. The Prophet (ﷺ) used to, when a funeral was brought to him, ask: "Does he have debt?" "Does he leave sufficient means to pay it?" If they said no, he would say: "Pray over your companion," and he would not pray over him.[[Recorded by al-Bukhari (2298) and Muslim (1619/14) from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to be brought a man who had died owing a debt, and he would ask: "Did he leave any surplus for his debt?" If it was reported to him that he had left enough to pay his debt, he would pray over him; otherwise he would say to the Muslims: "Pray over your companion." When Allah opened conquests for him, he said: "I am closer to the believers than their own selves. So whoever among the believers dies and leaves a debt, its settlement is upon me; and whoever leaves wealth, it belongs to his heirs."]] He (ﷺ) also informed that "martyrdom in the way of Allah expiates everything except debt."[[Recorded by Muslim (1886/120) from Abdullah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Being killed in the way of Allah expiates everything except debt."]] So the matter of debt is grave, and it is not permissible for a person to be careless about it.

Then He says: ﴿And none has a favour upon him that must be repaid﴾ [al-Layl 19]. That is, he does not give wealth as a reward for a past favour received from someone; no one has a bounty over him that would require him to give in return. Rather, he gives seeking the Face of Allah, and for this reason He says: ﴿except seeking the Face of his Lord, the Most High﴾ [al-Layl 20]. So he spends only seeking the Face of Allah; that is, seeking to reach the abode of Allah's honour, in which the vision of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is, takes place.

Commentary of Ibn 'Uthaymin (Tafsir al-Quran al-Karim) on surah 92, verse 21:

﴿And He will surely be well-pleased﴾ [Al-Layl: 21]. It means: Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will please him by giving him abundant reward. Allah has explained this in His saying: ﴿The example of those who spend their wealth in the way of Allah is like a grain that grows seven spikes, in each spike a hundred grains. And Allah multiplies for whom He wills. And Allah is All-Encompassing and All-Knowing﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 261].

We ask Allah to make us and you among those righteous, pure, and noble people, for He is capable of all things.
